is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae sensu stricto (M and S molecular forms), as stated in the title and abstract.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper genotypes the Vgsc L1014F (L995F) and L1014S (L995S) mutations (Abstract, Page 1).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 (Page 4) provides sample sizes (N) and allele frequencies with 95% CIs for S-form populations. Page 4 text provides allele frequencies and sample sizes for M-form populations (e.g., Benin N=5, 40% L1014F; Nigeria N=41, 19.5% L1014F; Cameroon N=48, 6.3% L1014F).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from 19 sites across 11 African countries: Senegal, The Gambia, Burkina Faso, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Benin, Nigeria, Cameroon, Gabon, Angola, and São Tomé and Príncipe (Table 1, Page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research article describing original field collections and molecular genotyping of kdr mutations.

sub_country_location.evidence: Table 1 (Page 3) lists 19 specific sampling sites including Kedougou, Bobo Dioulasso, Accra area, and others with coordinates.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Table 1 (Page 3) provides specific collection years for each site, ranging from 1998 to 2006, with most sites tied to a single year or a two-year range (e.g., Luanda area 2002-2003).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper mentions that a sub-sample of the HOLA-analysed sample had been previously genotyped by PCR for the L1014F allele in a 1998 study (Ref 2), but the current study presents a much larger, comprehensive dataset including new collections and L1014S genotyping.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype frequencies and sample sizes are provided in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study maps the distribution and frequency of Vgsc L1014F and L1014S kdr mutations in Anopheles gambiae (M and S molecular forms) across 11 countries in West and West-Central Africa. Samples were collected from 19 sites between 1998 and 2006 and genotyped using Hot Oligonucleotide Ligation Assay (HOLA) and allele-specific PCR (AS-PCR). The study provides baseline data on the spread of these resistance alleles across a wide geographical range.
